The identities hold for every differential graded right $A$-module $M$ and every integer $k$.

Let $(A, d)$ be a differential graded algebra. Then we have
$$
\Hom_{\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}}(A[k], M) =
\Ker(\text{d} : M^{-k} \to M^{-k + 1})
$$
and
$$
\Hom_{K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})}(A[k], M) = H^{-k}(M)
$$
for any differential graded $A$-module $M$.

reason: A dg-map A[k]→M is uniquely determined by the closed image of the free generator in degree −k. Chain homotopies identify two such maps exactly when their images differ by a coboundary, giving the indicated H^{-k}(M).
